first_failure.fix: OwnedValkey.start re-inspects the same verified CID and updates only the actual mapped host port. No product source or assertions relaxed.

actual_coverage.evidence: Actual SET/GET/FLUSHDB, actual owned container stop, connection failure, same CID restart, empty cache.

Independent provider committed accepted in FULL SQLite before the fixture PGDATA was stopped with pg_ctl immediate; actual PG socket connection failed. Actual Worker returned record_unavailable/unknown and business_action_success=false without any second POST. Same PGDATA restarted with crash recovery; fresh restricted Worker queried original intent and finalized real EIOS Action claim. effects=1, POST=1, GET=1, shared reserved_units=1, reservation=1.

The test itself SET a synthetic notification hint; actual Valkey FLUSHDB/stop makes that cache unavailable. Actual EffectDispatcher has no Valkey client and continues exclusively protected PostgreSQL polling and original-provider GET reconciliation. Final provider POST=1/GET=1 and quota=1. This proves the current PG Worker independence from real cache availability, not any production cache adapter reconnect or notification-delivery recovery.

ownership_and_cleanup.valkey: Only UUID-named containers created by this fixture; every stop/start/remove checked exact CID and nexloop.fault-owner label. No volumes or host mounts. finally docker rm --force completed, including the first failed test.
ownership_and_cleanup.pg: Only pg fixture mkdtemp nexloop-pg-* directory beneath tempfile.gettempdir; socket/data/PG_VERSION and pg_ctl status verified before stop. stopped_owned_pg restarted the same PGDATA in finally, then the pg fixture performed its own fast-stop and exact-directory cleanup. No production or persistent PG endpoint touched.
ownership_and_cleanup.runtime_identifiers: Transient CID and PGDATA paths were intentionally not persisted; ownership validation and finally execution are covered by the passing actual test code.

post_run_container_check.conclusion: No containers with this dedicated fault-test ownership label remain.

limitations: No real customer provider or model credentials were used.
Valkey is a disposable notification hint; actual effect Worker uses protected PG polling and does not rely on Valkey authorization or business state.
This does not establish the entire NX-017 failure matrix or deployment readiness.

No production Valkey notification adapter is assembled or exercised. The synthetic cache SET is performed directly by test code; adapter reconnect, replay and production notification loss remain unverified.
